items.cover: Nvidia CEO resigns amid federal probe[S3].
items.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned while federal investigators examined chips allegedly funneled to China.

• Huang resigned amid probes into relationships with an executive at Megaspeed and other Nvidia employees.
• Federal investigators examined Megaspeed for allegedly funneling Nvidia chips to China during the turnover.
• An expert who trained 1,000 security professionals noted personal connections can create espionage vulnerabilities.

Our read: Nvidia notes no public evidence links its security leadership changes to the Megaspeed investigation.

Your take: Should corporate security oversight include executive personal ties? Tell us in the comments.

items.text:
Helen Toner says we cannot trust AI CEOs to keep us safe.

• Toner says the OpenAI board failed to prioritize safety over profit.
• Paul Cristiano warns an AI takeover could cause mass death within months.
• Experts argue relying on individual executives for safety is insufficient.

Our read: Voluntary agreements depend on the same flawed governance structures that failed before.

Nvidia kept GPU prices high with circular financing deals.

• Nvidia absorbed excess TSMC wafers to sustain high GPU prices.
• GeForce GPU prices rose to more than 160% of MSRP.
• The strategy was described as a deliberate effort to prolong the AI boom.

items.text:
Elon Musk and over 115,000 signers are demanding Nvidia reinstate ousted CEO Jensen Huang.

• Huang resigned after confessing to an affair, and CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO.
• Over 115,000 signers, including Elon Musk and 5,965 Nvidia employees, petitioned for his return.

Our read: This rare public challenge shows how AI leadership disputes can quickly impact major chipmakers and tech markets.
